([[New Hampton, New Hampshire]]) | college = [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] (2013–2014) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * All-Big Ten Third Team ([[2013–14 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2014]]) * All-Big Ten Freshman of the Year (2014) * Big Ten All-Freshman Team (2014) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald’s All-American]] ([[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2013]]) }} '''Noah Vonleh''' (born August 24, 1995) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his freshman season at [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana University]]. He is considered one of the best prospects for the [[2014 NBA draft]].[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/nba/news/20130926/nba-draft-big-board-2014-andrew-wiggins/ 2014 NBA Big Board: Wiggins leads deepest draft in years][http://insider.espn.go.com/nbadraft/results/top100/_/year/2014 Chad Ford's Top 100 - 2014] ==High school career== Vonleh attended [[Haverhill High School]] in [[Haverhill, Massachusetts]]{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/blog/boston/high-school/post/_/id/3770/the-precious-noah-vonleh-experiments | title=The Precious Noah Vonleh Experiment | work=ESPN.com | date=December 24, 2010 | accessdate=June 22, 2014 | author=Hall, Brendan }} before transferring to [[New Hampton School]] in [[New Hampton, New Hampshire]]. As a junior in 2011–12, he averaged 16 points and nine rebounds per game. As a senior in 2012–13, he averaged 17 points, 12 rebounds and four assists per game, going on to earn McDonald’s All-American honors.[http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/noah_vonleh_858301.html Noah Vonleh Bio] On November 10, 2012, Vonleh signed a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] to play for [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana University]], turning down offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], and [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], among others. Upon committing to Indiana he said, "Their academics are good, they're the No. 1 team in the country and they've got another great class coming in next year."{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/8618967/no-8-senior-prospect-noah-vonleh-chooses-hoosiers | title=Noah Vonleh chooses Indiana | work=ESPN.com | date=November 11, 2012 | accessdate=February 3, 2013 | author=Finkelstein, Adam}} {{College athlete recruit start| 40 = no| year = 2013}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Noah Vonleh | position = [[Forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = Haverhill, Massachusetts | highschools = [[Haverhill High School]], [[New Hampton School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 9 | weight = 235 | commitdate = November 10, 2012 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | espn grade = 93 | 247 stars = 5 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = no | year = | rivals ref title = | scout ref title = | espn ref title = | rivals school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = | accessdate = April 8, 2014 | archivedate = | rivals archiveurl= | scout archiveurl = | espn archiveurl = | bball = yes }} ==College career== In his freshman season at [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], Vonleh was named to the 2014 All-Big Ten third team and All-Freshman team, as well as being named the Big Ten Freshman of the Year. In 30 games (29 starts), he averaged 11.3 points, 9.0 rebounds and 1.4 blocks in 26.5 minutes per game.[http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/noah-vonleh-1.html Noah Vonleh Stats] On April 3, 2014, Vonleh declared for the NBA draft, forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite web | url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/040314aad.html | title=Noah Vonleh Declares For NBA Draft | work=IUHoosiers.com | date=April 3, 2014 | accessdate=April 8, 2014}} ==Personal== Vonleh is the son of Samuel Vonleh and Renell Kumeh, and has two siblings. His paternal grandfather, Chief [[Blahsue Vonleh]], was [[Paramount Chief]] of the [[Doe District]], [[Nimba County]], Liberia, West Africa from 1920 until his death in 1947.[http://allafrica.com/stories/201405220536.html Liberia: NBA Bound - Grandson of Former Nimba Chief On Lakers, Celtics Radar] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/noah_vonleh_858301.html Indiana Hoosiers bio] {{Persondata | NAME = Vonleh, Noah | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = August 24, 1995 | PLACE OF BIRTH = Haverhill, Massachusetts | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Vonleh, Noah}} [[Category:1995 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Massachusetts]] [[Category:Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]]
